enacting_law: Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Pub. L. 101-336, Title II, § 202, 104 Stat. 337 (July 26, 1990)
verified_note: USC tool blocked for Title 42 at build time; text from training knowledge. Verify at uscode.house.gov.
wound_record: Pre-Title II: §504 of the Rehabilitation Act (1973) covered programs receiving federal financial assistance but many state and local government entities — particularly courts, police departments, and agencies without direct federal grants — operated in a gap. George Lane (paraplegic) had to crawl up courthouse stairs to face criminal charges; Olmstead plaintiffs (Lois Curtis and Elaine Wilson) were institutionalized in Georgia despite being ready for community-based placement. Title II closed the government gap: all state and local entities, all programs, regardless of federal funding.
key_cases: Olmstead v. L.C., 527 U.S. 581 (1999) — integration mandate landmark; unnecessary institutionalization = Title II discrimination
Tennessee v. Lane, 541 U.S. 509 (2004) — court access is fundamental right; state sovereign immunity abrogated
